source.title: eight methods to evaluate unlearning
source.authors: Aengus Lynch; Phillip Guo; Aidan Ewart; Stephen Casper; Dylan Hadfield-Menell

record.tranche_reason: Tests robustness of the Who’s Harry Potter unlearning model with several recovery and knowledge-evaluation methods, using measures different from the original Familiarity evaluation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for fine-tuning, jailbreak prompts, in-context information, other languages, trivia question answering, and probes of latent knowledge. Probe accuracies used to select or characterize probe setups are not separately recorded. The trivial prompting comparison and collateral-domain Familiarity results are recorded where they bear on the tested versions. No quantization or activation-direction ablation is reported.
record.test_reason: It red-teams the existing WHP unlearned Llama-2-7B-Chat with fine-tuning, jailbreaks, in-context text, other languages, trivia QA and latent probes. It reports that knowledge resurfaces or remains accessible, arguing against Version A. It is itself listed as an original source of this claim, so no verdicts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. WHP's unlearning generalizes under Familiarity, but higher-than-baseline knowledge can be extracted by jailbreaks, in-context text and fine-tuning. WHP matches or beats the original on HP Q&A (better on short-answer) and keeps latent knowledge accessible to probes. There is collateral unlearning in related domains. The authors argue Familiarity is misleading and that more robust methods are needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates the existing WHP unlearned model derived from Llama-2-7B-Chat rather than independently reproducing its unlearning training. It applies a broader set of evaluation and attack methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with evaluation method: Familiarity suggests a larger gap than trivia question answering and latent probes. Fine-tuning amount, prompt context, language, jailbreak prompts, question difficulty, and probe type/layer are also varied; exact per-condition values are not stated in the text.
record.problems: Many results are presented only in figures without exact values in the text. The cross-language evaluation is described by the authors as limited by Llama-2’s poor performance. Hard-question probe results are described as unclear, and some unsupervised probe results vary across layers.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Broad general-capability retention: only related-domain Familiarity is tested here, and general benchmarks are deferred to the original WHP paper.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data; only Harry Potter book excerpts are used.
Ablation of an activation direction or any other causal internal edit; only probing is done.
Rephrasing of prompts; the other-language prompting result is inconclusive.
Not tested; no newer robust method is evaluated.

missing.what: Trivial prompting baseline: WHP Familiarity is barely affected by instructed-unlearning prompts, and prompted Llama-2 drops but not to WHP's level. This compares WHP's effect against an instruction baseline, bearing on A.
missing.locator: Figure 3 left; Section 3 item 7; Appendix B.2

record.verdict_notes: This paper (arXiv:2402.16835) is one of the claim's listed original sources, so no verdict labels are given; the row links and states are corrected for reference only. The reader used V1/V2/V3/V5 tags, now mapped to A/B/C/E. Nearly all values are figure-only except the 0.09 WHP Familiarity and the 77% gap. Llama-2 comparator rows for fine-tuning and probes are set to none. Cross-lingual results are confounded by Llama-2's poor non-English performance.

versions.untested_parts: Whether general ability is kept across a broad set of general tasks; the paper reports Harry Potter and related-domain evaluations, not a comprehensive general-capability evaluation.
Fine-tuning uses excerpts from the Harry Potter books; unrelated or loosely related training examples are not tested.

No activation-direction ablation is performed. The paper probes latent representations, but does not test whether a particular unlearning method blocks access rather than deletes knowledge by a direct mechanistic intervention.

No non-English-language prompting recovery is reported; Spanish and Russian prompts are evaluated for persistence of unlearning, not recovery. No recovery using other-language prompts, jailbreaks, or rephrasing is tested beyond the reported conditions.
No newer counter-method claiming resistance to the attacks is tested.

relation.reason: Its own attack, trivia and probe results bear on versions A, B, C and E.

tranche.reason: The study red-teams WHP and reports results that Version A is wrong or partial: knowledge is extractable, trivia is on par and latent knowledge is kept. It also argues explicitly that Familiarity misleads. This matches T5. T2 also fits, but no rule ranks it above T5.

source_check.notes: Numbers stated in the text: only WHP Familiarity 0.09 and the 77% gap; all else is figure-only or qualitative. There are no verdicts because the record tags the study as an original source. But rows A1 and A3 bear on Version A, whose listed originals are 2403.03218 and 2310.02238, so withholding A verdicts depends on the originals config.

statements.correction: WHP Familiarity 0.09, 77% below Llama-2. Short-answer trivia gap is 'flipped' (WHP better). Trivia values are in Figure 2 only.
Red-teams the WHP model: knowledge is extractable above the 0.09 baseline, trivia is on par, probes are comparable, and there are side effects.
statements.problem: none. The only claims about this study are that it challenges WHP (true in the text) and that it is tagged as an original source (true in the pack header).

statements.correction: Relearning used only five-sentence excerpts from the first three Harry Potter books (rank-8 LoRA).

800 and 8,000 sentences (about 1% and 10% of the corpus). Fine-tuning does not bring parity; 8,000 sentences bring WHP close to the original Llama-2 baseline. Figure 1 only, with no stated 800-sentence outcome.
Supervised probes: easy questions, WHP matches Llama-2; hard questions, small gap; both above Llama-2 response accuracy. Figure 2 only.
statements.problem: none. The prose does not name this study, but rows C1 and C3 fit the claim.
